evaluation_methodology: 80/20 train/test stratified split on 1,524 samples combining Berlin SimRa crowdsourced cyclist records with TraCI synthetic surrogate safety kinematic encounters.
accuracy_interpretation: CAUTION: The 100% test accuracy is an artifact of synthetic-label partitioning where labels were generated using non-overlapping kinematic intervals (clearance < 1.02 m, 1.05–1.49 m, >= 1.52 m; decel < -2.4 m/s²). The test partition evaluates rule-boundary reconstruction fidelity rather than independent real-world predictive validity. It demonstrates that the gradient boosted decision trees perfectly learned the deterministic surrogate conflict rules, but MUST NOT be claimed as 100% real-world cyclist safety predictive accuracy.

synthetic_label_leakage.root_cause: Deterministic threshold boundaries in synthetic encounter generator resulted in separable feature intervals across the 3 classes.
synthetic_label_leakage.scientific_scope: Surrogate safety rule boundary convergence; not an empirical proof of real-world subjective risk perception.

limitations: Test partition measures surrogate threshold rule reconstruction rather than independent real-world prediction.

SimRa crowdsourced dataset lacks continuous LIDAR/radar lateral distance sensors; lateral clearance in SimRa traces was derived from ultrasonic sensor readings where available or calibrated synthetic proxy.
Model operates on macroscopic kinematic features (clearance, speed, deceleration, TTC); unmodeled environmental factors (road surface condition, weather, lighting) are not captured.
